title: Coefficient algebra for maps into a finite free algebra
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $B$ be a commutative $R$-algebra with an $R$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$, $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and fix a presentation $C=B[x_i:i\in I]/(f_k:k\in K)$ of a commutative $B$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Here $I,K$ are sets, and $(f_k:k\in K)$ denotes the ideal generated by the displayed family. Put $P=R[a_{ij}:i\in I,1\leq j\leq d]$ and let $\Psi:B[x_i:i\in I]\to B\otimes_RP$ be the $B$-algebra map $x_i\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes a_{ij}$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Write $\Psi(f_k)=\sum_j e_j\otimes c_{kj}$, with unique $c_{kj}\in P$, and set $D=P/(c_{kj}:k\in K,1\leq j\leq d)$. For every commutative $R$-algebra $A$ there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(D,A)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-alg}}(C,B\otimes_RA),$$
which sends $a_{ij}\mapsto\alpha_{ij}$ to $x_i\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes\alpha_{ij}$. The case $d=0$, necessarily $B=C=0$, is included, with $D=R$.

source.place: Tag 05Y6 (lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine), coefficient construction in the proof, in the relative B-algebra form used in BLR 7.6 Theorem 4 and Proposition 5(c),(d). The relations here are over B and the represented maps are over Spec B; this is the same basis-coefficient construction with the B-structure fixed.

proof.text: For every commutative $R$-algebra $A$, base change of the given basis gives an $A$-basis $(e_j\otimes1)_{1\le j\le d}$ of $B\otimes_RA$. Thus each element has a unique expression $\sum_j e_j\otimes\alpha_j$ with $\alpha_j\in A$. In particular, taking $A=P$ defines the coefficients $c_{kj}$ in the statement uniquely. Polynomial evaluation over $B$ gives the specified map $\Psi$; the tensor-algebra structure supplies the structural map $b\mapsto b\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, proof: basis-coefficient construction and inverse on affine tests; with the B-algebra structure fixed.

proof.text:
Write $Q=B[x_i:i\in I]$, $H=(f_k:k\in K)\subseteq Q$, $J=(c_{kj}:k\in K,1\le j\le d)\subseteq P$, and let $q:Q\to C$ and $p:P\to D$ be the quotient maps. For an $R$-algebra map $u:P\to A$, the tensor pushout property gives a $B$-algebra map $t_u:B\otimes_RP\to B\otimes_RA$ with $t_u(b\otimes z)=b\otimes u(z)$: use the maps $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $z\mapsto1\otimes u(z)$. The polynomial map $\theta_u:Q\to B\otimes_RA$ sending $x_i$ to $\sum_j e_j\otimes u(a_{ij})$ equals $t_u\Psi$, since the two $B$-algebra maps agree on every variable. Consequently
$$\theta_u(f_k)=\sum_j e_j\otimes u(c_{kj}).$$

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, proof: basis-coefficient construction and inverse on affine tests; with the B-algebra structure fixed.

proof.text:
By the $A$-basis of step 1, the displayed value is zero exactly when $u(c_{kj})=0$ for all $j$. Therefore $\theta_u$ kills every $f_k$ exactly when $u$ kills every $c_{kj}$. Killing a displayed family is equivalent to killing its generated ideal: an element of that ideal is a finite sum of multiples of family members, and a ring homomorphism sends each summand to zero. We obtain
$$H\subseteq\ker\theta_u\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad J\subseteq\ker u.$$

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, proof: basis-coefficient construction and inverse on affine tests; with the B-algebra structure fixed.

proof.text: Given $v:D\to A$ over $R$, put $u=vp$. Since $p(J)=0$, step 3 shows $\theta_u(H)=0$. Define $h_v:C\to B\otimes_RA$ by $h_v([g])=\theta_u(g)$ for $g\in Q$. This is well-defined: $[g]=[g^{\prime}]$ implies $g-g^{\prime}\in H$, hence $\theta_u(g)=\theta_u(g^{\prime})$. The formula preserves sums, products and the unit because $\theta_u$ does, and preserves $B$ because $\theta_u(b)=b\otimes1$. Thus $h_v$ is a $B$-algebra map with the claimed images of the variables.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, proof: basis-coefficient construction and inverse on affine tests; with the B-algebra structure fixed.

proof.text: Conversely let $h:C\to B\otimes_RA$ be a $B$-algebra map. Expand $h(q(x_i))=\sum_j e_j\otimes\alpha_{ij}$ uniquely by step 1. Polynomial evaluation yields the unique $R$-algebra map $u:P\to A$ with $u(a_{ij})=\alpha_{ij}$. Both $hq$ and $\theta_u$ are $B$-algebra maps agreeing on the variables, hence equal. They kill $H$, so step 3 gives $u(J)=0$. The formula $v_h([z])=u(z)$ is well-defined for $z\in P$, since changing $z$ by an element of $J$ does not change $u(z)$; it preserves ring operations and the $R$-structure. Starting with $v$, uniqueness of the basis coefficients recovers $u=vp$, and surjectivity of $p$ recovers $v$. Starting with $h$, the reconstructed map agrees with $h$ on every $q(x_i)$ and on $B$, hence agrees after precomposition with $q$ by polynomial uniqueness and then agrees with $h$ by surjectivity of $q$. The constructions are inverse.

source.place: Tag 05Y6, lemma-hom-from-finite-free-into-affine, proof: basis-coefficient construction and inverse on affine tests; with the B-algebra structure fixed.

proof.text: For an $R$-algebra map $s:A\to A^{\prime}$ the tensor pushout property gives the $B$-algebra map $t_s:B\otimes_RA\to B\otimes_RA^{\prime}$, $b\otimes a\mapsto b\otimes s(a)$. It sends $\sum_j e_j\otimes\alpha_{ij}$ to $\sum_j e_j\otimes s(\alpha_{ij})$. The coefficients of $sv$ are also $s(\alpha_{ij})$, so the bijections commute with $s$, which is the asserted naturality. If $d=0$, the empty basis forces $B=0$; a unital $B$-algebra is then the zero ring, so $C=0$ and $B\otimes_RA=0$. There are no variables or coefficients defining $D$, hence $D=R$. Both Hom sets are singletons, and the formulas above give their unique bijection. Empty $I$ or $K$ also require no change: the polynomial uniqueness and finite-sum ideal argument apply to empty families.
